newsitem.title: NORWAY: Cruise liner pulled off sandbank at Spitzbergen.
newsitem.headline: Cruise liner pulled off sandbank at Spitzbergen.

text.p: A German-owned cruise liner stranded off the Norwegian Arctic island of Spitzbergen was pulled off a sandbank early on Thursday by a Norwegian coastguard ship, an official said.

Elisabeth Aarsaether, spokeswoman for the governor's office at Longyear on Spitzbergen, said the Hanseatic, a 9,000-deadweight-tonne luxury liner, was freed at 3.45 a.m. (0145 gmt) by the coastguard ship Tromsoe.
"We had a deadline until 4 a.m. when the high water would be gone," she told Norwegian radio. "The ship is now being inspected."
The national news agency NTB said all 145 passengers were evacuated to the Tromsoe a few hours before the liner, with a crew of 115, was pulled free.
The report said the passengers, with an average age of 70, would be allowed to board the ship again should damage to the hull prove to be minimal.
Coastguards unloaded the ship's 480 tonnes of heavy fuel oil before dragging her free, NTB said.
The ship's owner, Hamburg-based Hapag-Lloyd AG, had originally planned to start evacuating passengers at 8 a.m. (0600 GMT).
The Bahamian-registered liner ran aground on Sunday in the Hinlopen fjord off Spitzbergen's north coast. It was on its way from Norway to Iceland via the rugged island.
Efforts to pull the Hanseatic free had been hampered by drifting ice which prevented rescue vessels from coming near her.
NTB said the wind changed late on Wednesday and pushed away the icefloes massed around the liner.
The passengers will be taken either by the Hanseatic or the Tromsoe to Longyear where they will be put on a charter flight to Hamburg, it said.
